round: windows-only guard enforced at every entry + released-artifact two-block run

finding.claim: README/README-zh/INSTALL told users that other platforms 'get a diagnostic instead of a half-working install'
finding.measured: with no guard, a simulated Linux platform reported a healthy `--doctor` (exit 0, "terminal": "wt") and `--run-windows` went on to make a real classify call
finding.verdict: the headline promise was false — a claim without a criterion
finding.method: node --import <preload that redefines process.platform> cli.mjs … (deterministic, offline; the preload only affects the first process, which is why the guard had to move to the entry that the user actually invokes)

fix.contract: one `[orchestrator] FATAL: Windows-only: …` line, exit 1, no Node stack, before host resolution / model calls / any state
fix.docs: INSTALL.md / INSTALL-zh.md now state the exact scope of the refusal

cases: a non-Windows platform is refused at the entry with one diagnostic line (and must not look like a healthy doctor report)
the platform-neutral entries still work on a non-Windows platform (--version prints the version pair; --install-deps reports already-present)
criteria.redCase: guard removed from a copy AND the copy resealed, then run under the fake platform ⇒ healthy --doctor exit 0, i.e. case 1 would fail. Real proof, not a claim.
